archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A winless New Orleans whose three losses all came down to the wire, with a top-ten offense dragged down by one of the league's most porous defenses, more a coin-flip team than a cellar dweller.

report.headline: Three near-misses hide a real offense and a familiar, leaky defense
report.take:
The Pelicans are 0-3, but the scores tell a gentler story: 120-123 to Indiana, 119-120 at Utah, 135-141 in overtime at Denver. The margin implies one win (winsByDifferential of 1, W vs Pt Diff of -1), and a Net Rtg of -3.2 ranks 18th, right where the site's Teams tab has them. This is not a team being blown out. It is a team that keeps scoring enough to win and then giving it back.

The offense is the genuine news. A 117.7 ORtg ranks 8th, up from 114.4 and an Off Rank of 21 last season, and it is built unusually. New Orleans takes the second-fewest threes in the league by 3PA Rate (34.2) and hits only 30.9% of them. It makes up for that by living at the line (FT Rate 34.2, 6th) and finishing inside, which is why its TS % (59.1) ranks 10th despite the cold shooting. Zion Williamson (65.5 TS %) and Derik Queen (65.9) are the engine, and the frontcourt grades an A while the backcourt (C) and wings (C-) lag.

The defense is the problem, and it isn't new. A 120.9 DRtg ranks 25th, the same Def Rank as last season's 26-56 team, and 2024-25's 21-61 group sat 29th. What is new is how it is breaking: opponents are not getting to the rim more often (Opp Rim Rate 30.4, exactly the league average), but they are converting 74.7% there, 8.5 points above the league. Centers have scored 30.67 a game against them, the most in the league and far above those players' own norms, and point guards are doing similar damage. Add a defense that forces few turnovers (Opp TOV % 11.9, 24th) and opponents get clean, finished possessions almost every trip.

Three games is a tiny sample, and the rim number in particular looks inflated by it. But this franchise's defensive ranking has been bad for two straight seasons, so the fair read is an improved offense paired with a defense that will stay below average. That profile wins its share of close games over 79 more, but it tops out around the fringe of the play-in, not above it.

strengths.title: Rim-and-line offense is top ten
strengths.body: The Pelicans score 124.67 a game (3rd) with a 117.7 ORtg (8th) despite barely shooting threes. Free throws and interior finishing carry it, which is a sturdier base than hot outside shooting. Some of that efficiency will cool, but last season's 114.4 ORtg suggests real improvement rather than a three-game mirage.

strengths.title: Frontcourt depth grades an A
strengths.body: Williamson and Queen are efficient high-usage finishers, and the backups have been even better in short minutes. Zion's 62 points on 65.5 TS % lead the team. Expect the bench bigs' gaudy numbers to fall to earth, but the group's quality looks real.

strengths.title: Losing close, not losing big
strengths.body: All three losses were one-possession or overtime games, and the differential implies a win the record doesn't show. Close-game results mostly even out, so the record should drift toward the margin. That points to wins, not a collapse.

concerns.title: Rim defense is collapsing early
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 74.7% at the rim, 27th and well above the league, and centers are scoring more against New Orleans than anywhere else. The volume of rim shots is normal, so the issue is contesting rather than containment. Some of it is small-sample noise, but a rank-25 DRtg matching last season's says the floor here is low.

concerns.title: Missi out thins the paint
concerns.body: Yves Missi, ranked 3rd among centers on the site with a 10.2 BPM, is listed out. That leaves Queen and DeAndre Jordan to anchor a defense already losing the interior. How long he is out is not in the sheet, but it matters most against Denver's and Memphis's glass-crashing frontcourts.

concerns.title: Guards and wings can't shoot
concerns.body: The team's 30.9 3P % ranks 22nd, and Jeremiah Fears has struggled badly (37.2 TS %, -15.6 BPM) in real minutes. Backcourt and wing grades of C and C- mean the perimeter isn't punishing defenses that pack the paint. Shooting should improve somewhat, but the low-volume approach caps the upside.

trend.note: Three games, three narrow losses, with the offense scoring in bunches every night and the defense giving it back. There is no shift yet, just a consistent profile.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, a Denver rematch and a real test in Memphis
weekAhead.body:
Four games, the first three at home, opening with a back-to-back. Denver returns after the overtime loss, and its A+ frontcourt and second-ranked rebounding are exactly the matchup that exposes a thin Pelicans interior without Missi. Sacramento the next night is the softest opponent on the slate: 0-3, 29th on the site, a -14.5 Net Rtg and a 122.5 DRtg. That is the clearest chance to get off the mark.

Atlanta is a real team (15.4 Net Rtg, 3rd) that forces turnovers (Opp TOV % 17.7, 4th), but its D- frontcourt and 29th-ranked rim defense invite exactly what New Orleans does best. The week closes in Memphis against a 3-0 side that leads the league in ORB %, a hard place to fix a rebounding and rim problem. A 2-2 week would be a fair result. 1-3 would sharpen the defensive questions.

keyMatchups.title: Zion against Atlanta's power forward defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta has allowed 33.67 points a game to power forwards, last in the league by margin over those players' norms. Its rim defense ranks 29th. If Williamson gets downhill, this is where the offense should peak.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against Denver and Memphis
keyMatchups.body: Denver ranks 4th and Memphis 1st in ORB %, and New Orleans is only middling on the defensive glass. Without Missi, keeping these two off the offensive boards decides whether the defense can get stops at all.

keyMatchups.title: Sacramento is the must-win
keyMatchups.body: The Kings sit 29th on the site with a 27th-ranked DRtg and have given centers far more than their norms. Queen should feast on the second night of the back-to-back. Losing this one would turn a bad-luck start into a real hole.

weekAhead.watch: Whether opponents' finishing at the rim drops from 74.7% toward the league norm, with Missi out.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the record to catch up to the margin. Three close losses are mostly noise, and an offense this efficient at the line and the rim should keep New Orleans competitive most nights. Expect some cooling from the 117.7 ORtg as the team's finishing regresses, though not all the way back to last season's 114.4, and a mild bounce in the 30.9 3P %. The defense is the cap. Its Def Rank has been 25th or worse three seasons running, so I'd project a DRtg settling around 115 to 119: better than the 120.9 now, still bottom-ten.

That adds up to a team clearly better than the last two seasons' 21 and 26 wins but short of a winning record, roughly 28 to 36 wins, on the fringe of the play-in conversation in the West. Missi's return and whether the guards stabilize are the levers that decide which end.
swingFactors: Perimeter shooting from the backcourt and wings

confidence.note: Three games; every rate is noisy and one center is out.
